messages:
maria: heads-up — after rolling edge-proxy 1.4.2 we started seeing a small but noisy class of SSE disconnects. clients report immediate EOF and a 1-2s reconnect loop. console shows ~2x active sessions briefly then drop.

alex: any error logs on the proxy side?

maria: here's the client-side snippet we captured (repro with curl too):
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -o -
# output: sometimes just a single "\n" then connection closed
```

sam: I saw this on staging earlier. looks like keepalive bytes are getting coalesced/truncated by the new flush path.

devops-bot: Deployment 2026-03-20T15:12:03 by @ops rolled edge-proxy v1.4.2 to canary.

julia: console-team — is there sampling/aggregation that could double-count sessions when reconnects are sub-second?

console-team: yes — current active-session gauge increments on socket open and decrements on explicit close. abrupt EOF path sometimes doesn't fire the decrement handler in the app -> spikes. we've been planning to switch to heartbeat-derived liveness for counts.

alex: can someone dump tcp/bytes on the proxy for a bad trace? I want to see whether last chunk is non-zero-length or actually zero-length closure.

maria: attached a tcpdump excerpt (hex) — looks like a two-byte keepalive then RST.

ben: RST suggests proxy is force-closing; maybe the new write coalescing hits a bug where we detect idle and close incorrectly. adding logging op_id->socket-state might help.

sam: quick experiment — downgraded a canary to 1.4.1 and the repro rate went to near-zero. suggests regression in 1.4.2.

julia: for telemetry/alerts: should we add a query for short-lived SSE sessions (<3s) and alert if rate increases 3x baseline? we can also annotate rollout.

console-team: agree. we'll add a dashboard panel: SSE short sessions per minute and a rollout tag to filter canary vs global.

alex: root cause theory: 1.4.2 changed the flush timer for small writes (optimizing throughput). some clients depend on an implicit newline flush to keep the SSE stream alive. the new coalescing delays that flush until >64B, server sees no heartbeat and kills.

maria: repro command to test the flush behavior:
```bash
# server side (toy) -> send single-byte "\n" every 500ms
# new proxy: connection closes after ~2s
# old proxy: stays open
```

ben: can we patch proxy to not consider small buffered writes as idle? quick fix: lower idle-close threshold when path is streaming. I'll open PR to 1.4.3 with a guard.

devops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03-sse-spike (canary roll). Assigned: @ben.

sam: also add a unit test that simulates very small periodic writes and ensures the proxy doesn't consider the connection idle.

julia: UX/rollout ask — if we push 1.4.3 hotfix, can console add an automatic annotation on the deployment so we can correlate short sessions drop post-fix?

console-team: yes, we can tag the deployment window and show before/after; will do.

maria: thanks. for now we'll hold global rollout and keep the canary at 1.4.1 until the patch lands. i'll keep posting traces here. :raised_hands:

alex: excellent. next steps: ben PR + canary revert or pause, console dashboard + alert, sam adds unit test, ops waits to promote.

ben: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/482 — guard added and unit. requesting review.

maria: verified on canary after PR applied: short-session spike down ~95%. looks good.

julia: moving to patch rollout channel for tracking. thanks everyone. :tada:
